item.title: Junior Up Helly Aa celebrates 70 years
item.description: The first Junior Up Helly Aa was held in 1956. Seventy years later, Junior Jarl Frankie Walterson is feeling excited about the big day along with his relatives Brydon and Bryan Peterson, who were Junior Jarls in 1966 and 1990 respectively.

item.title: Up Helly Aa 2026 – fire, folklore and a night to remember
item.description: Lerwick came alive once again as Up Helly Aa lit up the town with fire, music and tradition.

item.title: Why spring is the best-kept secret in Shetland
item.description: Five reasons why this often-overlooked season is one of the best times to experience Shetland.

item.title: 5 walks in Viking footsteps
item.description: If you dream of walking in Viking footsteps, Shetland rivals anywhere in the world. Here are 5 favourite walks to explore Viking heritage in the islands.

item.title: A Viking's view: what is it like being in an Up Helly Aa Jarl's Squad?
item.description: Regular contributor Ryan Nicolson was part of the Up Helly Aa Jarl's Squad in 2026, led by his father, Guizer Jarl Lynden Nicolson. Ryan offers an insider's insight into what it is like to be so involved in the festival.

item.title: Teaching at the edge of the world: life as a teacher in Fair Isle
item.description: Fair Isle is best known for its rugged beauty, world-renowned birdlife, and iconic knitwear, but it’s also home to one of the UK’s most geographically remote primary schools.

item.title: Run, Rabbit Run! The arrival of the Second World War in Shetland
item.description: Shetland's fascinating history is celebrated, from the Iron Age through to the modern era, via the Vikings. What is less well-known is that the first bombs to fall on British soil landed in Shetland's North Mainland in the mid-20th century.

item.title: Shetland dolphin watchers help conservation efforts
item.description: UHI Shetland and the Whale and Dolphin Conservation called on the public to share photos of Risso’s dolphins. Catherine Munro ventured out in the hope of spotting one of the beautiful marine mammals.

item.title: New reasons to visit Shetland in 2026
item.description: Shetland has never been short of reasons to get outside and explore, but 2026 is adding some particularly good new ones. From the depths of the voes to fine dining straight from the land, here’s a flavour of what’s happening in 2026. And trust us, this is just the start.

item.title: Strongest brothers discover fire, folklore and community spirit
item.description: Scotland’s strongest brothers, Luke and Tom Stoltman, travelled north to Shetland to witness the Up Helly Aa fire festival for themselves. They discovered the event is about much more than Vikings, flaming torches, and celebration. Up Helly Aa is underpinned by Shetland’s strong community spirit.
